title: Igbo-Ukwu bronzes
summary: At Igbo-Ukwu in south-eastern Nigeria, cistern digging in 1938 and Thurstan Shaw's excavations of 1959-60 uncovered bronze, copper, ceramic and glass artifacts, which Shaw thought came from a storehouse or shrine for ritual objects. Shaw dated them to the ninth century AD; newer radiocarbon work puts the final use of one site in the eleventh-twelfth century.

uncertainty.note: Shaw's radiocarbon dates gave a ninth-century result (his four clustered dates span the seventh to twelfth centuries at 2 s.d.); later AMS dating of a textile fragment gives the eleventh/twelfth century for Igbo Isaiah. Range here runs from the ninth to the end of the twelfth century.

as_recorded.value: eleventh/twelfth century CE (AMS date of a textile fragment, Igbo Isaiah)

where.modern_name: Igbo-Ukwu, Nigeria (find spot: Anozie family compounds); main collection National Museum, Lagos
where.historical_name: Igbo-Ukwu, in Igboland (pre-colonial; no state named in the sources)

importance.justification: A cache of bronze and copper objects with glass beads that, per the sources, predates European coastal contact by centuries.

sources.title: Igbo-Ukwu at 50: A Symposium on Recent Archaeological Research and Analysis
sources.author: Susan Keech McIntosh

reviewer_note: Least sure of the date: sources conflict (Shaw ninth century; 2022 work eleventh-twelfth century for the Igbo Isaiah deposit; the Igbo Richard burial and Igbo Jonah pit are unresolved). The pin is the town; the objects are not in Igbo-Ukwu. No claim made about trade routes.
